title: 'Defense of Japan 2026' White Paper Codifies Counterstrike Buildup, Record FY2027 Budget Request
detail: Japan's Defense Ministry released its annual white paper 'Defense of Japan 2026' on August 4, 2026, formally advancing the country's shift toward 'counterstrike capabilities' — including development of air- and ship-launched variants of the Type 25 anti-ship missile (deployed in Kumamoto Prefecture in March 2026 with 1,000km range), accelerated hypersonic-missile research, expanded AI and unmanned-systems programs, and incorporation of space into operational doctrine. The Ministry said it will request a record ¥8.9 trillion (~$56 billion) defense budget for FY2027. The paper frames rearmament as intertwined with industrial and economic policy, and cites China's expanding military reach in the Pacific as the primary driver.

media.caption: Japan's 2026 defense white paper codifies counterstrike and hypersonic buildup
